detailed_summary: The paper introduces a novel quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol called Bridge[d,q], which generalizes the SARG04 protocol to d dimensions and q bases. In this protocol, Alice and Bob each have only partial knowledge of the other's raw key, yet this partial information suffices to distill a definite mutual encryption key. The authors provide an experimental demonstration of Bridge[2,3], using three unbiased polarization bases switched by a single Pockels cell. The polarization basis switching method is applicable to any 3-basis QKD protocol and to other applications requiring fast manipulation of photon polarization qubits. The paper is 6 pages with 5 figures, indicating a concise presentation of both theoretical protocol and experimental results.
